newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fafer says shareholders not selling out.
newsitem.headline: Fafer says shareholders not selling out.

text.p: Belgian stainless steel company Fabrique de Fer (Fafer), commenting on Belgian media speculation, said on Friday it had no indications that its main shareholders had decided to sell their stakes in Fafer.

In a statement the company said that although it was studying strategic cooperation and synergy deals and/or partnerships, there was nothing at the moment that indicated these studies would have concrete results.
Fafer was commenting on a report in Belgian daily Le Soir which said Boel Group, which recently signed a 50/50 cooperation deal with Dutch Hoogovens, was considering selling Fafer.

Bourse-listed Fafer was being sold because its current size meant its long-term future could not be guaranteed and because of a lack of interest in Fafer from the younger generation of the Boel family which holds 50.5 percent of Fafer.
Le Soir said possible buyers included British Steel, Belgian-Luxembourg group Arbed/Sidmar and Usinor- Sacilor. In France, Usinor said it had no comment.

Fafer said that in recent months it had received various "signs of interest" or cooperation proposals. It added other companies approached it regulary. "At the moment there is nothing indicating (these developments) will have concrete consequences."

Earlier on Friday Usines Gustave Boel (UGB), also part of the Boel Group, said the main shareholders of Boel did not want to sell Fafer, adding they were thinking about the future of the company in an international context.
The shareholders did not exclude the possibility of cooperation with an international partner with a European view.

In April, Fafer -- with annual output of some 200,000 tonnes and sales of about 15 billion francs -- said net profit in the six months to December 21, 1996 fell to 111 million francs from 250 million as a result of disappointing macro-economic growth.
It said at the time it expected little improvement in the second half.

On the Brussels Stock Exchange shares in Fafer exceeded the permitted upper limit for movement on Friday as Le Soir's report sent bid/ask prices soaring. Fafer was indicated at 200,000 francs, almost double Thursday's 109,000 franc fixing price.
Fafer is quoted on the cash market, where prices are fixed twice daily. Prices are allowed to move by no more than five percent in any one direction at each fixing.
